title: PARSIFAL: Private and Robust Sign Federated Learning

problem.claim: Federated learning faces privacy leakage from model owners and model poisoning from adversarial data owners.

contributions.claim: PARSIFAL is a federated learning protocol addressing privacy leakage and model poisoning.
A poisoning detection module uses a novel sketch structure to efficiently detect gradients dissimilar to the majority of benign gradients.
A robust sign-gradient aggregation module mitigates poisoning effects, while privacy protocols based mainly on secret sharing protect detection and aggregation processes.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe PARSIFAL as novel and its sketch structure as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experimental results indicate that PARSIFAL achieves up to a 28% improvement in poisoning defense performance over recent baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning shares gradients instead of private data to support collaborative training.
The setting remains vulnerable to privacy leakage and malicious gradient poisoning.
PARSIFAL combines sketch-based poisoning detection, sign-gradient robust aggregation, and privacy protection.
Experiments report up to 28% improved poisoning defense over recent baselines.

source_observation.claim: The protocol combines detection, robust aggregation, and privacy protection within the federated learning process.

interpretation.claim: Security mechanisms may need to address both malicious updates and information exposure rather than treating them as separate concerns.

application.claim: For privacy-sensitive collaborative training, consider jointly designing update screening, robust aggregation, and privacy-preserving computation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination is effective across different datasets, attacks, or privacy requirements.

unknowns: Datasets, attack configurations, and evaluation metrics are unspecified.
The reported 28% improvement's exact metric and comparison conditions are unspecified.
Privacy guarantees, computational overhead, and scalability are unspecified.
Baseline identities and experimental protocol are unspecified.
